UMCG Radiology | 10 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate

Clinical context involves reassessment after a previously positive biopsy yielding ISUP GG 2, alongside a current PSA of 5.8 ng/mL and a historical PI-RADS 4 designation.

FINDINGS:
Prostatic dimensions total 54.0 mL. At the mid-gland level within the right peripheral zone, a discrete mass spans 12 x 10 x 8 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging exhibits pronounced restriction, mirrored by dark signal on the apparent diffusion coefficient maps. T2 sequences depict a sharply circumscribed hypointense region. Post-contrast evaluation highlights prompt, localized enhancement compared to adjacent tissue. Capsular integrity remains intact without seminal vesicle involvement. Pelvic lymph nodes show normal sizing and contour. Skeletal survey reveals no metastatic deposits.

IMPRESSION:
The right mid-peripheral zone harbors a PI-RADS 4 focus. Overall prostate volume registers at 54.0 mL, yielding a PSAD of 0.11 ng/mL/mL. The calculated csPCa probability stands at 0.48268548.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial evaluation began in late 2022 when a prostate-specific antigen level of 2.3 ng/mL triggered further investigation. A subsequent measurement of 4.1 ng/mL in November 2023 led to a targeted biopsy, which identified ISUP Grade Group 2 pathology. With the diagnosis confirmed and PSA advancing to 5.8 ng/mL, the patient was directed to the urology outpatient service.
